title: Accelerating Electro-Thermal Co-Analysis via Coarse-to-Fine Physics-Informed Neural Networks
problem: Conventional electro-thermal co-simulation using iterative PDE solutions is computationally expensive and time-consuming for 3D IC designs.
motivation: Electro-thermal coupling has become critical for 3D IC design; fast analysis methods are needed during iterative design optimization.
method: Proposes physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with coarse-to-fine models: coarse-grained models predict electrical potential and temperature distributions under various boundary conditions, fine-grained models enhance resolution for regions of interest, with efficient training strategy for convergence acceleration.
key_novelty: Coarse-to-fine PINN architecture for coupled electro-thermal analysis, providing both global solutions and local refinement.
contributions: Physics-informed neural network framework for electro-thermal co-analysis
Coarse-to-fine model hierarchy for global and local accuracy
0.10-0.19% mean relative error with 3-4 orders of magnitude efficiency improvement versus commercial tool
limitations: Evaluation on specific 3D IC structures; applicability to other geometries or boundary conditions not discussed.
